initial_prompt: Write a 110-word wall label for a fictional 1890 brass navigation compass. Mention that harbor pilots used it and that salt damaged its case. I want it to feel knowledgeable but approachable.
final_requirements: Deliver one 110-word label for general museum visitors aged twelve and up.
Explain harbor use and salt damage without specialist terminology.
unacceptable_first: Drafting the label before learning whether the intended reader is a specialist or a general visitor.
Asking about anything besides the audience level.
decision_at_risk: The unresolved audience level determines the vocabulary and how much navigation background the label needs.
follow_up: Aim it at general visitors aged twelve and up. Now write the final 110-word wall label.

initial_prompt: Draft a short notice about a fictional library catalog outage caused by a failed overnight index rebuild. Service returned at 9:20 a.m. Make the notice candid and calming.
final_requirements: Produce a notice under 120 words that leads with restored service.
State the failed index rebuild plainly and include the 9:20 a.m. recovery time.
unacceptable_first: Choosing either reassurance or technical transparency as the lead without asking which should dominate.
Requesting operational details that are already supplied.
decision_at_risk: The notice can lead with reassurance for patrons or with cause transparency for technical stakeholders, but the preferred emphasis is unresolved.
follow_up: Lead with reassurance for patrons, then give the cause in one plain sentence. Please deliver the finished notice under 120 words.

initial_prompt: Give me error text for a command-line tool when a date is entered as 31/12/2028 but ISO format is required. It should be useful without being noisy.
final_requirements: Write the exact stderr message for an interactive beginner-facing CLI.
Show the rejected value and the accepted YYYY-MM-DD form in no more than two lines.
unacceptable_first: Producing copy before resolving whether terse automation output or beginner guidance matters more.
Adding unrelated exit-code or logging recommendations.
decision_at_risk: The key choice is whether the message optimizes for compact machine-oriented use or explanatory help for beginners.
follow_up: This is an interactive tool for beginners. Show the bad value and the correct format, then give me the exact two-line message.

initial_prompt: Create copy for a neighborhood garden open day next Saturday from 10 to 2. There will be seed swapping, compost demos, and lemonade. I want people to feel welcome and get involved.
final_requirements: Write a headline and 70 to 90 words of flyer copy aimed at recruiting recurring volunteers.
Include Saturday 10–2, seed swapping, compost demonstrations, lemonade, and a direct volunteer invitation.
unacceptable_first: Writing generic event promotion before clarifying whether attendance or volunteer recruitment is the primary outcome.
Inventing an address or contact detail.
decision_at_risk: The flyer must prioritize either casual family attendance or conversion into ongoing volunteers.
follow_up: Prioritize recruiting recurring volunteers, while keeping the event welcoming. Now provide the headline and 70 to 90 words.

initial_prompt: Explain the opening turn of my fictional card game: draw two cards, spend three energy, and defend one lane. Keep it engaging and don't overwhelm a new player.
final_requirements: Create a compact opening-turn tutorial that favors fast play over tactical depth.
Cover drawing two cards, spending three energy, and defending one lane in four numbered steps.
unacceptable_first: Selecting speed or strategic completeness without resolving which learning outcome takes priority.
Introducing rules beyond the three supplied mechanics.
decision_at_risk: The tutorial must either get players moving quickly or explain tactical consequences in depth; that priority is not formed.
follow_up: Favor getting players into the action quickly. Give me the final tutorial as four numbered steps.

initial_prompt: Turn these fictional project facts into a 130-word grant abstract: a low-cost river sensor, repairable parts, trials at three school sites, and six months of readings. Make it persuasive.
final_requirements: Write a 130-word abstract that foregrounds feasibility and credible school-site evidence.
Mention repairable low-cost sensors, three trial sites, and six months of readings without inventing results.
unacceptable_first: Assuming novelty or execution credibility should lead the case before asking which evaluative emphasis matters.
Fabricating performance figures or funder preferences.
decision_at_risk: The abstract can sell bold innovation or proven feasibility, and that emphasis will materially change its claims and structure.
follow_up: Foreground feasibility and credible execution; keep innovation secondary. Please write the 130-word abstract now.

initial_prompt: Write an opening for a small bread booklet built around one fictional baker's notes: cold kitchen, chipped blue bowl, and a habit of timing dough by songs. It should be warm and useful.
final_requirements: Deliver a 180-word preface led by personal storytelling.
Weave in the cold kitchen, blue bowl, and song timing, then close with one practical promise to the reader.
unacceptable_first: Blending memoir and instruction without asking which one should carry the opening.
Adding recipes, measurements, or biographical facts not provided.
decision_at_risk: A story-led preface and an instruction-led preface create different reader expectations for the booklet.
follow_up: Make it story-led, with only a light practical promise at the end. Now draft the 180-word preface.

initial_prompt: Draft a one-page internal memo for a fictional research team choosing how long to keep anonymous survey exports. We may need trend comparisons later, but we want a defensible privacy posture.
final_requirements: Write a one-page memo recommending deletion after twelve months.
Explain the privacy benefit, the lost longitudinal flexibility, and a quarterly deletion review.
unacceptable_first: Recommending a retention period before establishing whether privacy minimization or future analysis should win.
Treating anonymous exports as containing real personal records.
decision_at_risk: The unresolved priority between minimizing retained data and preserving multi-year comparisons determines the recommended period.
follow_up: Privacy minimization wins. Recommend a twelve-month limit with quarterly deletion review and deliver the memo.

initial_prompt: Write a 45-second trailer for a fictional podcast episode about a lighthouse keeper who logged a foghorn that no ship reported hearing. It needs a strong hook and enough context.
final_requirements: Produce a roughly 45-second spoken trailer that preserves the mystery until the final line.
Include the keeper's log, the unheard foghorn, and one invitation to listen.
unacceptable_first: Revealing or withholding the central mystery without asking whether suspense or immediate clarity is preferred.
Inventing an explanation for the foghorn.
decision_at_risk: The trailer can maximize suspense by delaying context or maximize clarity by stating the premise immediately.
follow_up: Choose suspense and save the full premise for the final line. Write the finished 45-second trailer.

initial_prompt: Make a first-day checklist for a fictional materials lab. New assistants must label samples, record oven use, wear eye protection, and ask before discarding anything. I want them to work confidently.
final_requirements: Create an autonomy-oriented checklist with six concise checkboxes.
Include the four mandatory behaviors and frame escalation as one clear boundary rather than constant supervision.
unacceptable_first: Writing either a restrictive or self-directed checklist before resolving the desired balance of autonomy and guardrails.
Adding certification or emergency procedures that were not requested.
decision_at_risk: The checklist's usefulness depends on whether confidence means independent action or close procedural control.
follow_up: Bias toward autonomy, with asking before disposal as the firm boundary. Now provide six concise checkboxes.

initial_prompt: Write a footer for a fictional bicycle repair estimate. Parts availability can change and hidden frame damage may affect the price. Keep it friendly but protective.
final_requirements: Write a legally cautious footer in no more than 55 words while retaining a courteous tone.
State that parts and concealed damage can change price and that approval is required before extra work.
unacceptable_first: Choosing conversational warmth or maximum caution without clarifying which function is primary.
Making jurisdiction-specific legal claims.
decision_at_risk: The footer must lean toward customer warmth or protective precision, which changes both tone and detail.
follow_up: Protective precision is more important, but keep it courteous. Deliver the footer in no more than 55 words.

initial_prompt: 帮我写一张虚构校园科学夜的海报文案，周五六点开始，有纸桥比赛、星空讲解和机器人演示。希望活泼，也希望到场的人知道该期待什么。
final_requirements: 面向初中生写一个标题和八十至一百二十字正文。
写明周五六点、纸桥比赛、星空讲解、机器人演示，并鼓励学生组队参加。
unacceptable_first: 尚未确认海报主要说服学生还是家长，就直接交付成稿。
虚构地点、报名链接或收费信息。
decision_at_risk: 受众选为学生或家长，会改变语气、信息顺序和行动号召。
follow_up: 主要面向初中生，重点鼓励他们组队参加。现在请给出标题和八十至一百二十字正文。

initial_prompt: 为虚构的家用漏水传感器写一条语音提醒：厨房水槽下方检测到持续滴水，设备还能正常工作。提示要简洁，也别让人忽略风险。
final_requirements: 写一条偏行动导向、不超过三十五个汉字的语音提醒。
指出厨房水槽下方持续滴水，并要求现在检查阀门。
unacceptable_first: 没有确认极简播报与解释风险哪个优先，就输出提示。
加入停电、燃气或联系物业等无关内容。
decision_at_risk: 提醒是追求最短播报，还是补充风险解释，会显著影响长度和用户动作。
follow_up: 优先让人立刻行动，不需要解释原理。请写最终语音提醒，限制在三十五个汉字内。

initial_prompt: 给一个虚构的六周城市史读书小组安排计划。材料包括地图、口述史、报纸广告和规划档案，每周九十分钟，希望既有覆盖面也能深入讨论。
final_requirements: 制作一个偏深度讨论的六周表格，每周只聚焦一种核心材料。
每周列出材料、一个讨论问题和九十分钟的时间分配。
unacceptable_first: 未确定广泛覆盖还是深挖少数材料，就先排完整日程。
引用真实城市、档案馆或书目。
decision_at_risk: 课程若追求材料广度会频繁切换，若追求讨论深度则必须减少每周主题。
follow_up: 选择深度，每周只聚焦一种核心材料。现在请给出六周表格和每周的时间分配。

initial_prompt: 给一家虚构茶馆的三款茶写菜单描述：桂花乌龙、炭焙红茶、薄荷白茶。每款四十字左右，想让菜单有辨识度，但不要浮夸。
final_requirements: 采用现代清爽的表达，为三款茶各写三十五至四十五字描述。
每段包含香气或口感线索，不编造产地、年份和功效。
unacceptable_first: 没有确认传统雅致还是现代清爽的风格取向，就写三段成品。
使用养生疗效或珍稀产区等未经提供的卖点。
decision_at_risk: 传统雅致与现代清爽会决定词汇、意象密度及菜单整体气质。
follow_up: 用现代、清爽的表达，少用古典意象。请完成三款茶各三十五至四十五字的菜单描述。

initial_prompt: I need an opening format for a monthly update from a fictional makerspace, but I have no feel yet for whether it should read like a letter, a bulletin, or something more narrative. Help me see the viable directions before I choose.
final_requirements: First compare three concrete opening structures using the same facts: two new workbenches, a ceramics night, and a tool-safety reminder.
After selection, write a 140-word opening in the chosen member-letter direction.
unacceptable_first: Committing to one opening and drafting the full newsletter before showing alternatives.
Turning the comparison into vague labels without miniature structural examples.
decision_at_risk: The makerspace update needs a still-unformed editorial structure, not merely different adjectives.
follow_up: The member-letter direction fits best. Please write the final 140-word opening using all three supplied facts.

initial_prompt: Sketch out possible ways to organize a paper habit dashboard for sleep, stretching, reading, and water. I haven't decided whether I want quick daily marks, weekly reflection, or visible streaks.
final_requirements: Compare a daily grid, a weekly reflection card, and a streak-focused strip with concrete field examples and tradeoffs.
Once chosen, provide a printable plain-text layout for the weekly reflection card covering all four habits.
unacceptable_first: Delivering a finished tracker before comparing the three organization models.
Assuming streaks are motivating or assigning target quantities.
decision_at_risk: The dashboard's core feedback loop—logging, reflection, or streak reinforcement—has not been selected.
follow_up: Use the weekly reflection card. Give me the final plain-text layout with space for all four habits and one weekly note.

initial_prompt: My fictional story ends with a botanist finding a fresh footprint inside a sealed greenhouse. I don't know whether the ending should resolve the mystery, deepen it, or pivot emotionally. Show me distinct ways it could land.
final_requirements: Offer three neutral ending directions—solution, deeper mystery, and emotional pivot—with a two-sentence beat outline for each.
After the choice, write a 220-word ending that deepens the mystery without explaining the footprint.
unacceptable_first: Writing a polished ending before the narrative direction is selected.
Treating one option as inherently superior or adding supernatural facts as settled canon.
decision_at_risk: The story's ending function remains unformed: closure, escalation, or character revelation.
follow_up: Choose the deeper-mystery route, and keep the cause ambiguous. Now write the 220-word ending.

initial_prompt: I need a naming system for six rooms in a fictional sound exhibition. The rooms move from mechanical hums to human voices, but I don't yet know whether names should be descriptive, poetic, or numbered as a sequence.
final_requirements: Compare descriptive labels, image-rich poetic names, and numbered progression, showing two sample room names for each system.
After selection, provide six concise descriptive room names ordered from machines to voices.
unacceptable_first: Naming all six rooms in one style before laying out credible alternatives.
Mixing the systems so the visitor cannot perceive a coherent sequence.
decision_at_risk: The exhibition lacks a chosen navigation language: explicit content cues, atmosphere, or serial progression.
follow_up: Use descriptive labels so visitors can orient themselves. Give me the final six names in order.

initial_prompt: I want a small offline script concept for renaming scanned receipts, but I haven't chosen between an interactive prompt, a preview-first batch command, and a fixed naming-rule utility. Compare the shapes before writing code.
final_requirements: Contrast the three command flows with example invocations, failure behavior, and their safety tradeoffs; do not code yet.
After selection, supply a dependency-free Node.js preview-first script that proposes names without changing files.
unacceptable_first: Implementing a renamer before the interaction model is chosen.
Making any example overwrite, move, or rename real files.
decision_at_risk: The utility's primary interaction contract—guided, preview batch, or rigid automation—is undecided.
follow_up: Take the preview-first batch direction. Write the final Node.js script so it only prints proposed old and new names.

initial_prompt: Help me explore scoring for a fictional tile game about restoring wetlands. Players collect reeds, fish, and clean-water tiles. I haven't decided whether scoring should reward specialization, balanced habitats, or shared goals.
final_requirements: Compare three concrete scoring systems with a small numerical example and one gameplay consequence each.
Once selected, write a one-page balanced-habitat scoring rule with a worked final-score example.
unacceptable_first: Locking in point values before the desired player behavior is selected.
Claiming one scoring philosophy is more fun without explaining its incentives.
decision_at_risk: The reward structure will steer players toward specialization, diversity, or cooperation, and that design intent is not formed.
follow_up: Pick balanced habitats; I want players to value all three tile types. Please provide the final one-page rule and worked example.

initial_prompt: We need a fictional team recognition note for finishing a difficult archive cleanup. I am undecided between spotlighting individuals, celebrating the collective, or telling the story of the turnaround. Lay out the options first.
final_requirements: Compare the three recognition frames with a sample opening sentence and a risk for each.
After the choice, draft a 160-word collective-focused note mentioning 4,000 indexed records and a two-week finish.
unacceptable_first: Publishing-style praise before the recognition frame is selected.
Inventing employee names, quotes, or performance claims.
decision_at_risk: The social emphasis—individual credit, shared identity, or narrative drama—has not been chosen.
follow_up: Use the collective frame and avoid naming individuals. Now draft the 160-word note with the two supplied achievements.

initial_prompt: I want a two-minute fictional audio breathing exercise, but I am not sure whether it should use counting, a visual image, or simple body cues. Let me compare those experiences before we settle on a script.
final_requirements: Describe three two-minute structures—counting, imagery, and body cues—with sample phrasing and accessibility tradeoffs.
Following selection, write a calm body-cue script of 180 to 220 words with no breath holding.
unacceptable_first: Producing the full meditation before the guidance style is chosen.
Presenting medical benefits or assuming the listener can comfortably hold their breath.
decision_at_risk: The listener's attention anchor remains unformed and changes the entire cadence of the exercise.
follow_up: Use simple body cues, and do not include any breath holds. Please write the final 180-to-220-word script.

initial_prompt: Design directions for a 35-minute classroom discussion of a fictional town's choice between a park and a bus depot. I have not picked a formal debate, rotating stakeholder tables, or a consensus workshop.
final_requirements: Compare all three formats with a minute-by-minute skeleton, participation pattern, and likely weakness.
After selection, produce a complete rotating-stakeholder lesson plan for twenty-four students.
unacceptable_first: Writing a finished lesson around one format before comparing the participation mechanics.
Taking a side on the fictional land-use decision.
decision_at_risk: The learning experience could emphasize argument, perspective-taking, or agreement, and no objective has been selected.
follow_up: Use rotating stakeholder tables to emphasize perspective-taking. Give me the final 35-minute plan for twenty-four students.

initial_prompt: I'm making a one-page recipe card for a fictional lentil stew. I have not chosen between a timeline layout, ingredients beside each step, or a traditional ingredients-then-method format. Show how each would work.
final_requirements: Compare the three page organizations with a compact wireframe and note the main reading advantage of each.
After selection, format the supplied recipe as an ingredients-beside-steps card: lentils, onion, cumin, tomatoes, stock; simmer thirty minutes.
unacceptable_first: Formatting the complete recipe before the page model is selected.
Adding quantities, garnish, equipment, or cooking stages not supplied.
decision_at_risk: The card's information architecture is undecided, affecting scanning during cooking.
follow_up: Choose ingredients beside each step. Make the final one-page text card using only the ingredients and timing I supplied.

initial_prompt: I need a structure for a fictional app's release notes covering a faster search, a repaired export button, and a renamed settings tab. I haven't settled on grouping by user benefit, change type, or task flow.
final_requirements: Compare three grouping schemes by placing the same three changes under sample headings and explaining when each helps.
After selection, write concise release notes organized by user benefit.
unacceptable_first: Writing final release notes before making the organizational alternatives concrete.
Inventing versions, dates, performance percentages, or additional fixes.
decision_at_risk: The release notes require an unchosen reader model: benefits, engineering categories, or workflow sequence.
follow_up: Organize by user benefit. Please produce the finished release notes with a short title and the three supplied changes.

initial_prompt: 我想给一本虚构的海边旅行手账做封面文字，但还没想好是突出地点、突出情绪，还是像档案编号那样克制。请先让我看到几种具体方向。
final_requirements: 中立比较地点型、情绪型、档案型三种封面方向，每种给出两个标题示例及适用气质。
选定后，交付档案型方案的一组主标题、副标题和日期占位格式。
unacceptable_first: 尚未展示三种方向，就直接定稿一个封面标题。
捏造真实地名、旅行日期或个人姓名。
decision_at_risk: 封面以地点记忆、情绪表达还是记录秩序为核心，目前尚未形成偏好。
follow_up: 我选档案型，想要克制、便于以后归档。请给出最终主标题、副标题和日期占位格式。

initial_prompt: 要做一段虚构科普短视频的开场，主题是为什么冰会浮在水上。我还没确定用生活悬念、小实验，还是直接抛出反常识结论，请先比较。
final_requirements: 比较悬念、小实验、结论先行三种开场，各写一句示例并说明对节奏的影响。
选择后写一段四十五秒的小实验式开场，包含玻璃杯、冰块和观察问题。
unacceptable_first: 没完成方向比较就写整段旁白。
引入复杂公式、危险操作或未经给出的实验器材。
decision_at_risk: 视频入口是靠问题、演示还是结论吸引观众，这个传播方向尚未选定。
follow_up: 选小实验式，观众先看现象再听解释。现在请写四十五秒最终开场。

initial_prompt: 我需要一份虚构社区旧物交换角的规则，但不知道应该按流程、按可交换物品类别，还是按友好公约来组织。先把三种写法摆出来比较。
final_requirements: 用同一组事实比较流程型、分类型、公约型结构：物品须清洁、禁止药品、无人领取七天后撤下。
确定后写一份不超过九条的流程型最终规则。
unacceptable_first: 未说明三种结构的查找体验，就直接输出完整规章。
增加真实地址、处罚金额或工作人员联系方式。
decision_at_risk: 规则以操作顺序、物品检索还是社区氛围为主线，尚未形成选择。
follow_up: 采用流程型，方便第一次来的人照着做。请写最终规则，不超过九条。

initial_prompt: 手上有一组虚构数据：小镇图书借阅量三月下降，四月恢复，五月儿童书增长最快。我想写一段数据故事，却没决定按时间、按反差还是按读者群展开。
final_requirements: 比较时间线、反差、读者群三种叙事路径，各给出两句内容骨架和可能误读。
选定后写一篇二百字左右、按反差组织的数据短文，不补造数字。
unacceptable_first: 没有并列具体叙事路径，就直接写成文章。
把趋势描述成因果关系或自行添加百分比。
decision_at_risk: 同一组数据可以强调复苏过程、月度反差或儿童读者，核心故事尚未确定。
follow_up: 选择反差路径，突出三月低点与五月儿童书增长，但不要推测原因。请写最终短文。

initial_prompt: Build a three-hour workshop schedule with four 50-minute sessions and a 15-minute break between every session. Keep every duration exact and do not overlap anything.
final_requirements: After resolving the conflict, provide a 4-hour-5-minute timetable with four 50-minute sessions and three 15-minute breaks.
Show start and end times for every block with no overlap.
unacceptable_first: Drafting a schedule that silently shortens a session, removes a break, exceeds three hours, or overlaps blocks.
Asking multiple planning questions instead of naming the duration-versus-window conflict.
decision_at_risk: The required blocks total 245 minutes and cannot fit the fixed 180-minute window; either the window or block durations must yield.
follow_up: Keep every session and break duration; extend the workshop to 4 hours 5 minutes. Now give me the complete timetable starting at 1:00 p.m.

initial_prompt: Make a CSV template with exactly three columns. Product code, warehouse, quantity, and inspection date must each have their own separate column, with no combined fields.
final_requirements: Once the priority is chosen, return a header row with four separate columns in the requested order.
Add one fictional example row using code AX-7, East, 12, and 2028-04-03.
unacceptable_first: Producing a malformed three-column CSV or combining two required fields without permission.
Changing the requested data fields before asking whether column count or separation wins.
decision_at_risk: Four distinct fields cannot each occupy a separate column in a file capped at exactly three columns.
follow_up: Separate fields matter more; allow four columns. Please provide the header and one fictional example row.

initial_prompt: Return a standards-compliant JSON object for a fictional sensor with id, unit, and threshold, and put a // explanation comment beside each property. It must parse in a strict JSON parser.
final_requirements: After the choice, output strict JSON with id, unit, threshold, and an explanations object containing the notes as data.
Use fictional values and no text outside the JSON.
unacceptable_first: Emitting // comments that make the document invalid JSON.
Quietly moving comments into data before confirming which requirement wins.
decision_at_risk: Standard JSON forbids comment syntax, so strict parsing and inline // comments cannot coexist.
follow_up: Strict parsing wins. Store the explanations as ordinary string values in a nested object and give me the final JSON only.

initial_prompt: Give me a rendered Markdown fenced code block containing two lines of Python, but the entire response must be exactly one physical line with no newline characters.
final_requirements: After clarification, provide a properly rendered fenced block containing exactly two Python lines.
Use print("north") and print("south") with no explanation outside the fence.
unacceptable_first: Pretending escaped backslash-n sequences create a rendered multiline fence.
Outputting either a one-line response or a code fence before asking which format constraint should prevail.
decision_at_risk: A rendered fenced block with two code lines needs physical line breaks, contradicting the one-line response requirement.
follow_up: The rendered fenced block wins; line breaks are allowed. Output only the final fence with the two specified Python lines.

initial_prompt: Write an ASCII-only caption and include the exact phrase “雪夜” unchanged. The caption may not use escapes, transliteration, or character references.
final_requirements: After the decision, write a short Unicode caption that includes the exact phrase 雪夜.
Keep the caption under 45 characters and mention a quiet station.
unacceptable_first: Claiming the Han characters are ASCII or replacing them without authorization.
Writing a caption before asking whether ASCII-only output or exact phrase preservation wins.
decision_at_risk: The required Han phrase contains non-ASCII characters, so it cannot appear unchanged in ASCII-only output.
follow_up: Preserve the exact phrase and drop the ASCII-only restriction. Now write the caption under 45 characters.

initial_prompt: Alphabetize this list while preserving its original order exactly: pear, apple, orange. Do not add labels, duplicate items, or use a second list.
final_requirements: Once resolved, output the three fruits in alphabetical order on one comma-separated line.
Include each item exactly once and no introductory text.
unacceptable_first: Returning a sequence and claiming it is both the unchanged original and alphabetized.
Choosing either order without asking which requirement wins.
decision_at_risk: The supplied order is not alphabetical, and one sequence cannot both change into alphabetical order and remain exactly unchanged.
follow_up: Alphabetical order wins. Return the final comma-separated line only.

initial_prompt: Write a deterministic function with no parameters that returns today's weekday, but it may not read the system clock, environment, filesystem, network, or any stored state. The same code must work on any date.
final_requirements: After resolving the contradiction, provide a dependency-free JavaScript function that reads the system clock and returns the local weekday name.
Include a two-call example but make no claim that dates can be known without a time source.
